passage: On the metro home to Rajouri Garden, Gurleen read Nilesh's apology for the third time. "I skipped your exhibition for a cricket match. It made you feel unimportant. I'm sorry, that was on me." It was a good apology. It didn't fill the empty chair where she'd hoped he would be. She typed, "Thanks for saying that. I need a little time." She added nothing else; her thumb hovered, and she put the phone away. Across the city, Nilesh read it in his hostel room. He wanted to reply, "How much time?" He wanted to send a sad face. Instead he wrote, "Of course. I'm here when you're ready," and went to make dinner.

qa.q: What did Nilesh skip Gurleen's exhibition for?
qa.a: He skipped it for a cricket match.

qa.q: Why does Gurleen ask for time even after a good apology?
qa.a: The apology was good, but it didn't fill the empty chair, so she still needs time before she feels ready.

qa.q: What did Nilesh do well while waiting?
qa.a: He held back from asking "How much time?" or sending a sad face, and simply said he'd be there when she was ready.

qa.q: What might Nilesh be feeling as he goes to make dinner?
qa.a: He is probably a bit anxious and impatient, but he chooses to bear the wait instead of pushing her.

grounding: Shows a young woman thanking a friend for his apology but asking for time, and him accepting the wait without pushing or sulking.

passage:
"Asma replied," Karthik said, holding up his phone. "'Thanks for saying that. I need a little time.'"
"That's good, no?" Asif said from the stove.
"Is it? How much time? A day? A month? Should I call her?"
"Karthik. You apologised properly. Now she gets to take her time."
"But I said sorry. I did everything right."
"Saying sorry doesn't mean she owes you a quick 'it's fine'."
Karthik flopped onto the sofa. "So I just... wait?"
"You wait. No sad emojis. No 'are we okay yet?'" Asif handed him a plate. "And no sulking. That's pushing too, just quieter."
Karthik stared at the message. "Fine. I'll wait." He put the phone face down, screen away from him.

qa.q: What did Asma's reply say?
qa.a: "Thanks for saying that. I need a little time."

qa.q: What is Karthik worried about after reading the reply?
qa.a: He worries about how long it will take and wants to rush it, feeling that because he said sorry things should be fine.

qa.q: What advice does Asif give about waiting?
qa.a: Wait without pushing: no sad emojis, no "are we okay yet?", and no sulking, since that is pushing too.

qa.q: How might Asma feel if Karthik called right away?
qa.a: Asma might feel pressured, as if her need for time didn't matter, which could undo the good apology.

grounding: Shows a young woman asking for time after an apology, and the one who apologised learning to wait without pushing or sulking.

passage:
I remember the evening Kunal finally apologised properly. We were sitting by the college lake.
He said, "I told everyone your secret because I wanted to look interesting. It made you feel betrayed. I'm sorry."
It was a good apology. I could feel that. But my chest still hurt.
I said, "Thanks for saying that. I need a little time."
He nodded. He didn't argue or look annoyed. He just said, "Okay. Whenever you're ready."
For two weeks, he didn't push. No sad messages, no sulking in class. He just said hi, normally.
I'm Rajni, and I think that waiting did more for us than the apology itself.

qa.q: Where were Rajni and Kunal sitting when he apologised?
qa.a: By the college lake.

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling after Kunal's apology?
qa.a: Rajni felt grateful for the apology but still hurt, which is why Rajni asked for a little time.

qa.q: What made the waiting period work?
qa.a: Kunal accepted Rajni's need for time without pushing or sulking, just saying hi normally for two weeks.

qa.q: What might Kunal have been experiencing during those two weeks?
qa.a: He was probably anxious and hopeful, but he held back from pushing, respecting that forgiveness was not owed on schedule.

grounding: After a real apology, a young adult asks for time, and the friend who apologised waits patiently without pushing or sulking.

passage:
Hostel warden's note, girls' block, Thursday

Last week Sonali and Bidisha, who share room 12, had a serious falling out after Bidisha read Sonali's diary. Today Bidisha apologised properly in the common room; I was nearby.
Sonali listened, then said, "Thank you for saying that. I need some time."
Bidisha's face fell a little. I could see she wanted it fixed today. But she nodded, and said, "Okay."
Later I found Bidisha sitting alone on the stairs. I told her that forgiveness isn't owed on a timetable, and that waiting without pushing or sulking is part of the apology.
She said she'd try. I'll check on both of them next week.

qa.q: What did Bidisha do that caused the falling out?
qa.a: She read Sonali's diary.

qa.q: What was Sonali feeling when she asked for time?
qa.a: She felt grateful for the apology but still hurt, needing time before she could forgive.

qa.q: What did the warden do that helped?
qa.a: The warden explained to Bidisha that forgiveness isn't owed on a timetable and that waiting patiently is part of the apology.

qa.q: What was Bidisha experiencing on the stairs?
qa.a: She was disappointed and anxious, wanting everything fixed right away.

grounding: A warden records a young woman asking for time after an apology, and helps the one who apologised accept the wait without pushing.

passage:
Friday night

Uma apologised today. A real one, not a "sorry if". She said, "I told your parents about the concert, and it got you in trouble. I'm sorry."
I felt something unclench. But I wasn't ready to hug and go for chaat.
So I said, "Thanks for saying that. I need a little time." My voice shook a bit.
Uma said, "Okay, that's fair." And then she went back to her side of the lab and didn't look sad at me or send twenty messages.
That's what's making me want to forgive her, honestly. She's letting me take my time. Maybe next week. — Parveen

qa.q: What did Uma tell Parveen's parents about?
qa.a: About the concert.

qa.q: What was Parveen feeling after Uma's apology?
qa.a: Parveen felt some relief, something unclenching, but still hurt and not ready to forgive fully.

qa.q: Why does Uma's response help Parveen move towards forgiving her?
qa.a: Uma accepted the need for time without pushing, sulking or sending lots of messages.

qa.q: What might Uma be experiencing as she goes back to her side of the lab?
qa.a: She is likely anxious but respectful, tolerating the wait because she knows Parveen needs time.

grounding: After a real apology, a young adult asks for time, and the friend who apologised accepts the wait without pushing or sulking.
